THE ACTUAL WORKSHEET

Exactly what you’ll print.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Dot-to-dots chain two skills: number order and line control. Your child says each number aloud while connecting, so counting and drawing practice each other. The picture reveal is its own reward.

  • Number order 1–10
  • Saying numbers while drawing
  • Straight connecting lines
  • Finishing the full loop
HOW TO USE IT

Three easy steps.

  1. Warm up in the air

    Trace the shape of the line in the air with a big arm movement before pencil touches paper. Handwriting starts in the shoulder.

  2. Start at the green dot

    Every guide has a green start dot and a star to finish on. Say the movement out loud together — “up, around, around”.

  3. Praise the staying-on, not the speed

    Slow and wobbly on the line is exactly right. Speed comes on its own once the movement is easy.

TEACHING TIPS

Little things that help.

Little and often

Five happy minutes on one sheet beats twenty strained ones. One or two rows is still a real session.

Left-handers are first-class here

Tilt the paper slightly the other way and let the hand sit below the line — nothing else changes.

Keep the pencil chunky

Triangular pencils or chunky crayons build the right grip without reminders.
